content: Is the name of docs4#Set.mem_setOf_eq actually correct?
Looks correct to me. How else would you name it?
Didn't we replace all the _eq lemmas with _iff lemmas anyway?
{ x | p x } is called setOf, I think
Not this one :frowning:
oh okay it's fine. I thought it was a lemma of the form x∈Sx \in Sx∈S implies x∈Tx \in Tx∈T when S=TS = TS=T.
I should look at the type more carefully next time :)
I would like to revive this topic. We currently have duplicate declarations docs#Set.mem_ofPred and docs#Set.mem_ofPred_eq. Which one should we keep?

/poll Which name to keep
Set.mem_ofPred
Set.mem_ofPred_eq
The issue here is that Set.mem_ofPred_eq has the @[defeq] attribute, while Set.mem_ofPred cannot have it. See also #mathlib4 > `=` vs `↔`
It's unfortunate that the Lean 3 feature of allowing dsimp to use Iff.rfl was never ported (or at least, never merged)
When I use the simp? tactic I will always get Set.mem_setOf_eq when it could be Set.mem_setOf with no loss of functionality. Thus one must go, and it is the longer-named lemma
The issue is in dsimp, not simp. The iff version doesn't work in dsimp
Well, #42692 builds and it only uses the equality version (iff version deprecated)
Was this PR generated by a regex? I see many changes of mem_ofPred_eq to mem_ofPred but because of the size of the PR it's very difficult to see quickly if anything else is happening.

Yes, the first commit was simply replacing Set.mem_ofPred_eq with Set.mem_ofPred in VS Code's search and replace; the rest are just fixing errors related to the name change to Set.mem_ofPred

/poll In #42692 what should the name of the remaining lemma be?
mem_ofPred
mem_ofPred_eq
I find this poll quite confusing, and suggest this alternative:

/poll Which of these should be the target non-deprecated API:

  • mem_ofPred_eq : (x ∈ {y | p y}) = p x, mem_ofPred : (x ∈ {y | p y}) ↔ p x (status quo)
  • mem_ofPred : (x ∈ {y | p y}) ↔ p x (drop the Eq version)
  • mem_ofPred_eq : (x ∈ {y | p y}) = p x (drop the Iff version)
  • mem_ofPred : (x ∈ {y | p y}) = p x (drop the Iff version and rename)
I will not accept the status quo because the current Set.mem_ofPred (with iff) is strictly redundant. Sorry.
I have been continually updating #42692

Eric Wieser said:

/poll Which of these should be the target non-deprecated API:

Why, for any reason, should the status quo be maintained in this case?

I think the bigger picture here is having to chose between:

  1. Always write Iff lemmas as Eq instead if they hold definitionally (to allow them to be used with dsimp)
  2. Never use Eq lemmas for propositions (because this confounds attempts to search with loogle / guess names). Optionally teach dsimp to handle Iffs.
  3. Have two copies of every lemma.
Your PR locally implements option 1, but I'm not sure it makes sense to apply globally.

What's the status of "teach dsimp to handle Iffs"? This was tried back then; see lean4#2678 (for the issue) and lean4#2679 and lean4#3973 for @Thomas Murrills's attempts to address this. Can you update us on the current status, Thomas? How messy were things; how much work would you expect fixing this to be?

Let me gently point out that mathlib maintainers are making the final call about decisions here (not you, Jeremy). But I appreciate the reminder that something should be fixed. If that's easily possible, fixing dsimp and then (2) sounds ideal from my armchair perspective. In any case, I've added it to the maintainer's backlog, so this will be discussed in due time.

My attempts back then required tweaking many, many simp calls in mathlib, to the point that I think it was not a reasonable change. But some things have changed since then, so it’s probably worth another shot…!

I think it could maybe be done in two steps now:

  1. Allow passing Iff lemmas to dsimp
  2. Auto-tag Iff.rfl proofs with defeq
Maybe things are even moving in the direction of 2 not being desirable.
